subject: POC: real-time assistant - tokenization, streaming & rerank semantics
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@orionai.com>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: real-time assistant POC - tokenization & streaming concerns

Hi Steph / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the concise walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a few technical questions we need to resolve before the PoC kickoff:

Recap:
- Goal: build a real-time assistant for our sales reps that can summarize live chat transcripts, call notes, and callouts from our internal KB.
- Scale: expect ~80 concurrent reps in week 1; target 250 concurrent within month 1 if PoC successful.
- Data sensitivity: PII in transcripts; need controls for redaction and optional private deployment.

Questions (high priority for our infra/security team):
1) Chat vs completions: we heard the chat API preserves turn metadata which we like (better for tool-calling). For streaming transcripts where we push partial user utterances, do you recommend chat streaming or completions streaming for lowest latency and predictable token billing? Any gotchas with function/tool-calling while streaming?

2) Tokenization differences: our transcripts contain a lot of short tokens (URLs, emojis, unicode). How does Redwood handle tokenization across model families (gpt-like vs LLM-open) — will the token counts in your console match what we see locally? We need a guide to estimate max_tokens for both request and response to avoid truncation.

3) stop / max_tokens interplay: when the assistant streams partial outputs, how do stop sequences apply? If we stream and then send a stop token from our client, does Redwood truncate remaining buffered tokens or still bill generation up to the next boundary?

4) Embeddings + reranker: we plan to surface top-5 KB passages and then run a lightweight reranker. Is it better to request embeddings from the same model family as the generator for semantic alignment? Any recommendations on batch size and typical latency for a 512-dim / 1536-dim embedding on a dedicated instance?

5) Auth / routing: for the PoC we can use API keys, but security prefers mTLS or VPC peering. Can Redwood support mTLS for Private deployments? Also, can we route traffic to a dedicated pool in us-east for lower latency?

I've attached our network diagram and sample transcript snippet. If you can answer the above and share a short PoC runbook + SOW draft, we can schedule an internal security review for next Wed.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Price
Head of Integrations, Orion AI

Attachments: orion-net-diagram.png (image), sample-transcript.txt (text)

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: real-time assistant POC - tokenization & streaming concerns

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram; good context. Short answers here and a proposed PoC plan attached (redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf) — diving into each item below.

1) Chat vs completions (streaming):
- Recommendation: use the chat endpoint for the PoC. Chat semantics preserve role metadata and are first-class for function/tool calling.
- Streaming behavior: we stream token chunks as they’re generated; function calls can stream the arguments as JSON. If you need the generator to execute functions deterministically, we recommend non-streamed function invocation for the final call, or use a short streaming preview then confirm with a non-streamed finalize call.

2) Tokenization:
- We rely on model-specific tokenizers; counts in Redwood Console match the model tokenizer used for a given model. For planning, use our token-estimation guide (attached in the PoC plan) — it includes heuristics for URLs, emojis, and UTF-8 sequences.

3) stop / max_tokens while streaming:
- Stop sequences are applied server-side as soon as they are detected in the generation stream; we will stop emitting tokens once a stop is matched. Billing: we bill tokens actually generated (streamed or buffered). If a stop arrives client-side and you request a cancel, we accept the cancel and stop generation, but any tokens already generated and emitted are billed.

4) Embeddings + reranker:
- Recommendation: use a dense-embedding model from the same family for better semantic alignment, but you can use a smaller embedding model for indexing + a larger model for reranking if latency allows.
- Batch sizing: start at batch=64 for 1536-dim vectors; expect 20–60 ms per vector on Dedicated depending on GPU (A10 vs A100); we include perf profiles in the plan.

5) Auth & routing:
- PoC: API keys are fine. Private (VPC/on-prem) supports mTLS and KMS integrations; we'll include an options matrix in the SOW.
- Routing: yes — policy-based routing to a dedicated us-east pool is supported and can be locked to the deal.

Next steps (proposed):
- We’ll prepare a short SOW + runbook (attached).
- Suggested PoC timeline: 3 weeks (week 0 security review, week 1 implementation, week 2 load + quality checks).
- Can you confirm security meeting availability on Wed Apr 4th at 10am ET?

CC: Ben and David to provide any deeper infra notes below.

Cheers,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf, SOW-draft-orion.docx

Subject: Re: Follow-up: real-time assistant POC - tokenization & streaming concerns

Hey Samantha — quick technical clarifications from our ops side that will help sizing and secure onboarding: 

- Token accounting: if you run local pre-tokenization (e.g., to enforce user quotas), be aware that model tokenizers may split differently (esp. with emojis/zero-width joiners). For conservative quotas, apply a 1.2x multiplier to your local counts for gpt-like models.

- Streaming cancel semantics: client cancel vs server-side stop: server stops when a stop sequence is matched or when the request is cancelled. If you cancel from the client mid-stream, the server may have already generated tokens that are in-flight; those are billed. If determinism matters for reranker inputs, we recommend writing the streamed preview only for UX and performing a final non-streamed call to produce the canonical output that feeds the reranker.

- Function/tool calling while streaming: possible but fragile for deeply nested JSON arguments; we recommend streaming to show progress but finalizing the function call in a short non-streamed confirm to ensure full argument serialization.

- Embeddings batching & rerank: for the PoC, plan for 64–128 batch for embeddings ingestion. Reranker can be served as a small gen model that scores candidates — keep the reranker narrow (top-20 candidates) to keep latency <150ms for interactive flows.

- Auth: for expedited PoC we’ll issue scoped API keys with short TTLs and IP allow-listing. For broader rollout we’ll map to mTLS or Private deployment with VPC tunnels.

I'll be available on the Wed security call to walk through the network requirements.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
